question: For an unreceipted legacy runs.json whose prior runtime-import history cannot be proven, should doctor suppress automatic import to prevent resurrection while preserving the file for explicit recovery?
rationale: No deterministic inspection can distinguish a never-imported source from a stale source whose rows were previously imported and later deleted; choosing between automatic recovery and replay prevention is an upgrade-policy decision.

options.title: Prefer no resurrection
options.body: Record durable no-replay provenance, retain the ambiguous file, and provide a doctor warning and explicit recovery path for operators who know it contains unique state.

options.title: Prefer automatic recovery
options.body: Import an ambiguous source whenever canonical rows are empty, accepting that deleted historical runs can reappear.

options.title: Pause the migration change
options.body: Keep the PR open until a different provenance signal can reliably distinguish the two histories without either tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Prefer no resurrection
recommendation.body: Record durable no-replay provenance, retain the ambiguous file, and provide a doctor warning and explicit recovery path for operators who know it contains unique state.
